text:
The data point to August 2022, for these reasons:

- Headline CPI was 8.48% year over year, which matches the July 2022 reading published in August (8.5%).
- Core CPI was 5.91%, also matching July 2022.
- The fed funds rate was 2.33%, which fits the July 2022 average of 2.33%.
- The unemployment rate was 3.5%, matching July 2022.
- Payroll growth of about 437k over three months fits the May–July 2022 average.

The market returns are less clear for August. US large-cap equity fell 3.2% over the month, but the S&P 500 rose in July and fell about 4% in August, so the one-month figure may reflect month-end timing or a different cut-off. The 10-year yield at 3.11% and the 2-year at 3.46% also fit late August, when the 10-year was about 3.1% and the 2-year about 3.4%. The 10-year-minus-2-year spread of -0.35 is consistent with that too. Treasuries falling 3.1% over the month fits August, and the 12-month equity return of -11.2% matches the S&P 500 at the end of August 2022.

CPI for July would have been published in mid-August, so the snapshot most likely describes the end of August 2022.
